newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fifty bidders interested in Australia govt railway.
newsitem.headline: Fifty bidders interested in Australia govt railway.

text.p: Fifty potential buyers have expressed interest in AN, the Australian government's loss-making rail operation, Transport Minister John Sharp said on Sunday.
Sharp added he was confident that the upper house of the Australian parliament, dominated by parties generally opposed to privatisation, would pass the necessary legislation.
"We've had tremendous interest from the private sector," he said on Seven Network television. "Some 50-odd people have expressed an interest in buying AN."

AN, formerly Australian National, is the remainder of the federal government's rail operations left after profitable elements were merged with some state services to form the National Rail Corporation in 1993.

Track ownership has also been separated from AN and what is left is a collection freight and passenger services burdened with more than A$1 billion in debt and expected to lose about A$250 million in the fiscal year to June 30.
The Liberal-National government said last year it would sell AN, which the former Labor administration, under pressure from rail unions, had kept in public hands .
Sharp said the government was aiming for the upper house, the Senate, to pass the legislation in the sittings that will run from August to November.
However, the government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate.

Of the non-government parties, the Australian Democrats and Greens, almost invariably oppose privatisations and the Labor opposition, which sold many government enterprises when it was in office, has lately adopted a more leftist stance in most policy areas.
"Even with opposition from the Labor Party and the Democrats it's possible that we can muster sufficient support in the Senate to get it through," Sharp said.
Assuming the Greens do not back the privatisation, the only source of the two votes that the government needs is a pair of independents.
The government also wants to sell its 40 percent of the National Rail Corporation.
